description: The control vector the Python interp exporter writes and the Rust runtime steers with: an artifact directory holding a safetensors image of per-block f32 directions, plus a manifest.json beside it

layout.vector.safetensors: the directions; the only file either Rust reader parses as tensors
layout.manifest.json: provenance and the model identity, written by interp/manifest.py

constraints: every block tensor is 1-D f32 and they share one width
at least one block tensor is present
index is a 0-based decoder block, and block 0 is steerable
the manifest's width equals that shared width, and its layers list the indices present
no direction holds a non-finite value

notes.block_numbering: index is the 0-based decoder block whose output residual the direction is added to. This has always been the block itself and never the block plus one, in both the exporter and the reader. What changed at R10 is that index 0 became legal: the retired llama.cpp layout named the same tensors direction.<layer> and refused 0, because repeng trains key k on the output of block k and upstream describes that numbering as 1-based, leaving the first block unsteerable for a reason this backend does not share. The counterpart is schemas/probe_artifact.json's 'layer', which is 0-based in the same sense, so the two interp artifacts now agree.
notes.prefix_was_renamed_deliberately: direction. became block. in the same change that dropped the index floor, so an image written before R10 fails to load rather than loading. It would in fact have loaded correctly, because no index moved -- which is the problem: nothing would then have distinguished a pre-R10 file from a post-R10 one if the numbering later did move. The rename makes the format's generation visible at the reader.
notes.why_not_gguf: This artifact was GGUF until R10, and the format was not this repository's to choose: llama.cpp read the file as --control-vector-scaled. R9 gave the harness an HTTP endpoint and R10 retired the llama.cpp steering path, leaving one reader here. The tensors then go where every other tensor in this repository goes, through runtime/src/checkpoint.rs Image under forbid(unsafe_code), and runtime/src/gguf.rs was deleted with the last artifact that needed it. GGUF survives only in training/export/ and common/serving.py's quant_from_name, which produce and name what llama.cpp serves.
notes.manifest_is_advisory: A vector whose manifest is missing or unreadable still loads; harness/src/main.rs warns and skips the identity check. This is the opposite of schemas/probe_artifact.json's sidecar, which is mandatory, and the asymmetry is the point: that sidecar carries the layer, the site and the decision threshold, so a probe without it is unusable, while this manifest carries only provenance and an identity check. interp/steering/wiring.py is stricter than the Rust reader and refuses a directory without one, because a scorecard run records the manifest into its report.
notes.model_hint_is_gone: The retired GGUF carried controlvector.model_hint, a model type rather than an identity, and no reader ever read it. Nothing replaced it: the manifest already carries model_id, model_revision and model_hash, and source.model_type where the extractor recorded one.
notes.layer_range_at_load: manifest.layer_range records the band directions were extracted over, and is null when none was given. It is provenance, not a filter. Selecting a subset at serve time is --control-vector-layer-range on the harness, which drops the blocks outside it as the image is read, so the forward pass sees only what it must add. llama.cpp spelled the same idea --control-vector-layer-range.
notes.comparison_is_semantic: The committed fixtures are compared by parsed content -- tensor names, widths, values, and the manifest's keys and values -- never byte for byte. safetensors is pinned, but a version bump may legitimately change header key order or padding, and the manifest carries 'created' and 'git_sha', which differ on every regeneration; a byte comparison would report either as exporter drift.
notes.float_exactness: Fixture values are chosen to be exact in f32, so a round trip through the writer and the Rust reader is an equality comparison and needs no tolerance.
notes.non_finite_directions: A non-finite direction is added to every position's residual, so it turns the whole stream to NaN and the model emits noise instead of failing. The exporter refuses it and names the block, rather than leaving the reader to discover it as output nobody can interpret.
